<h3 id="vad-quality-best-practices" class="hide-from-toc" data-text="Understanding VAD parameters and their impact on quality" tabindex="-1">Understanding VAD parameters and their impact on quality</h3>

<p>When using automatic VAD, two key parameters control how audio is
segmented into speech turns before being sent to the model:</p>

<ul>
<li><strong><code translate="no" dir="ltr">prefixPaddingMs</code></strong>: The amount of audio to include <em>before</em> speech
is detected. This &quot;look-back&quot; ensures the model captures the full
onset of speech, including the first syllable which may start before
the VAD triggers. A value of <code translate="no" dir="ltr">0</code> may cause the beginning of words to
be clipped.</li>
<li><strong><code translate="no" dir="ltr">silenceDurationMs</code></strong>: How long the server waits through silence
before ending a speech turn. This determines how tolerant the system
is of natural mid-sentence pauses (e.g., thinking, breathing, or
clause boundaries).</li>
</ul>

<h4 id="impact_of_silencedurationms_on_audio_quality" data-text="Impact of silenceDurationMs on audio quality" tabindex="-1">Impact of <code translate="no" dir="ltr">silenceDurationMs</code> on audio quality</h4>

<p>The <code translate="no" dir="ltr">silenceDurationMs</code> value directly affects the size and completeness
of audio chunks the model receives for processing:</p>

<ul>
<li><strong>Recommended (500ms–800ms):</strong> Provides a good balance—the model
receives complete, contextually rich audio chunks while keeping latency
reasonable. The server&#39;s internal default is approximately 800ms.</li>
<li><strong>Too low (e.g., 100ms–200ms):</strong> The system ends speech turns during
natural pauses, splitting a single utterance into multiple small audio
fragments. The model receives these fragments individually, losing
cross-fragment context and resulting in lower transcription and response
quality.</li>
<li><strong>Too high (e.g., 2000ms+):</strong> The system waits a long time after the
user stops speaking, increasing perceived latency before the model
responds.</li>
</ul>

<h4 id="best_practices_for_manual_client-side_vad" data-text="Best practices for manual (client-side) VAD" tabindex="-1">Best practices for manual (client-side) VAD</h4>

<p>When you disable automatic VAD and manage <code translate="no" dir="ltr">activityStart</code>/<code translate="no" dir="ltr">activityEnd</code>
signals from your own client-side voice detection, be aware that the
server&#39;s built-in audio buffering mechanisms are bypassed. This means:</p>

<ol>
<li><strong>No pre-speech buffer:</strong> The server no longer prepends audio before
the detected speech start. Your client should include sufficient audio
context before sending <code translate="no" dir="ltr">activityStart</code>.</li>
<li><strong>No silence tolerance:</strong> The server acts immediately on your
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">activityEnd</code> signal with no additional wait. If your client-side VAD
uses an aggressive end-of-speech threshold (e.g., 200ms of silence),
speech may be cut off mid-sentence during natural pauses.</li>
</ol>

<p>To preserve audio quality with manual VAD, use an end-of-speech silence
threshold of at least <strong>500ms</strong> in your client&#39;s voice activity detector.
Thresholds below this value often cause fragmented audio that degrades
transcription and model response quality.</p>

<h2 id="token-count" data-text="Token count" tabindex="-1">Token count</h2>

<p>You can find the total number of consumed tokens in the
<a href="/api/live#usagemetadata">usageMetadata</a> field of the returned server message.</p>

<h2 id="media-resolution" data-text="Media resolution" tabindex="-1">Media resolution</h2>

<p>You can specify the media resolution for the input media by setting the
<code translate="no" dir="ltr">mediaResolution</code> field as part of the session configuration:</p>
<div><devsite-selector data-ds-scope="code-sample">
<section><h3 id="python_19" data-text="Python" tabindex="-1">Python</h3><div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded syntax="Python"><code translate="no" dir="ltr"><span class="devsite-syntax-kn">from</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nn">google.genai</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-kn">import</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-n">types</span>

<span class="devsite-syntax-n">config</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-o">=</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-p">{</span>
    <span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"response_modalities"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-p">[</span><span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"AUDIO"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">],</span>
    <span class="devsite-syntax-s2">"media_resolution"</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">:</span> <span class="devsite-syntax-n">types</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">MediaResolution</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-n">MEDIA_RESOLUTION_LOW</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">,</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-p">}</span>
</code></pre></devsite-code></section>
<section><h3 id="javascript_19" data-text="JavaScript" tabindex="-1">JavaScript</h3><div></div><devsite-code><pre class="devsite-click-to-copy" translate="no" dir="ltr" is-upgraded syntax="JavaScript"><code translate="no" dir="ltr"><span class="devsite-syntax-k">import</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">{</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nx">GoogleGenAI</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">,</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nx">Modality</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">,</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nx">MediaResolution</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">}</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-kr">from</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-s1">'@google/genai'</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">;</span>

<span class="devsite-syntax-kd">const</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nx">config</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">=</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">{</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">    </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nx">responseModalities</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">[</span><span class="devsite-syntax-nx">Modality</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-nx">AUDIO</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">],</span>
<span class="devsite-syntax-w">    </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nx">mediaResolution</span><span class="devsite-syntax-o">:</span><span class="devsite-syntax-w"> </span><span class="devsite-syntax-nx">MediaResolution</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">.</span><span class="devsite-syntax-nx">MEDIA_RESOLUTION_LOW</span><span class="devsite-syntax-p">,</span>

</code></pre></devsite-code></section>

<h2 id="limitations" data-text="Limitations" tabindex="-1">Limitations</h2>

<p>Consider the following limitations of the Live API
when you plan your project.</p>

<h3 id="response-modalities" data-text="Response modalities" tabindex="-1">Response modalities</h3>

<p>The native audio models only support `AUDIO  response modality. If you need the
model response as text, use the <a href="#audio-transcription">output audio transcription</a>
feature. </p>

<h3 id="client-authentication" data-text="Client authentication" tabindex="-1">Client authentication</h3>

<p>The Live API only provides server-to-server authentication
by default. If you&#39;re implementing your Live API application
using a <a href="/gemini-api/docs/live#implementation-approach">client-to-server approach</a>, you need to use
<a href="/gemini-api/docs/ephemeral-tokens">ephemeral tokens</a> to mitigate security
risks.</p>

<h3 id="maximum-session-duration" data-text="Session duration" tabindex="-1">Session duration</h3>

<p>Audio-only sessions are limited to 15 minutes,
and audio plus video sessions are limited to 2 minutes.
However, you can configure different <a href="/gemini-api/docs/live-session">session management techniques</a> for unlimited extensions on session duration.</p>

<h3 id="context-window" data-text="Context window" tabindex="-1">Context window</h3>

<p>A session has a context window limit of:</p>

<ul>
<li>128k tokens for <a href="#native-audio-output">native audio output</a> models</li>
<li>32k tokens for other Live API models</li>
</ul>

<h2 id="supported-languages" data-text="Supported languages" tabindex="-1">Supported languages</h2>

<p>Live API supports the following 97 languages.</p>
<aside class="note"><strong>Note:</strong><span> <a href="#native-audio-output">Native audio output</a> models can switch between
languages naturally during conversation. You can also restrict the languages
it speaks in by specifying it in the system instructions.</span></aside>
